item.title: [threat-intel] Social engineering attacks on open source developers are escalating
item.description: <p>North Korean hackers spent weeks socially engineering an Axios maintainer through a fake Slack workspace, a cloned company identity, and a fabricated Microsoft Teams call that tricked him into installing a RAT posings as a software update. They used the access they gained to inject malware into npm packages downloaded 100+ million times a week. item.title: [threat-intel] Iranian cyber activity hits US energy, water, and government networks
item.description: <p>U.S. government agencies on Tuesday warned American organizations about ongoing cyber activity targeting OT and PLC devices, including those manufactured by Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley, across multiple critical infrastructure sectors. The activity has been attributed to Iranian-affiliated APT actors seeking to disrupt operations in the United States. item.title: [threat-intel] Cybercriminals move deeper into networks, hiding in edge infrastructure
item.description: <p>Attack activity is moving toward infrastructure outside endpoint visibility. Proxy networks support a wide range of operations, edge devices serve as initial access points, and GenAI speeds up how attackers assemble and rebuild their tooling. Lumen’s 2026 Threatscape Report describes this pattern in criminal and nation-state activity. &#8220;Threat intelligence is needed to find the adversary as early as possible and as close to the point of origination as possible,&#8221; said Chris Kissel, IDC VP, Security &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/08/large-botnets-campaigns-attack-activity/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/08/large-botnets-campaigns-attack-activity/">Cybercriminals move deeper into networks, hiding in edge infrastructure</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>
